neighbours.label: the word 'both' (on both sides, both X and Y, both of them), as opposed to the same sentences with each, every, the two, or plain coordination
fire: Voters on both ends of the spectrum disliked the plan.
The recipe works well with both fresh and frozen berries.
Our neighbours have two dogs, and both of them bark at night.
The treaty was signed by both countries in May.
He plays both guitar and piano in the band.
Make sure to check both sides of the form before you sign it.
The museum was closed on both days we tried to visit.
Researchers interviewed both parents and teachers for the study.
quiet: Voters at each end of the spectrum disliked the plan.
The recipe works well with fresh or frozen berries.
Our neighbours have two dogs, and each of them barks at night.
The treaty was signed by the two countries in May.
He plays guitar and piano in the band.
Make sure to check every page of the form before you sign it.
The museum was closed on the days we tried to visit.
Researchers interviewed parents and teachers for the study.
